name: H5N1 bird flu
value: Three dairy-linked US cases; no human spread
summary: Washington's H5N1 cases this autumn are linked to dairy cattle; no human-to-human spread reported
state: ECDC's tracker records that two more Yakima County, Washington, residents were confirmed with H5N1 as of 1 Nov, one of whom died, bringing the county to three human cases; an October case followed exposure to infected dairy cattle (ECDC). Health officials said the risk to the public is low (CP24, 2 Nov). Searches to 19 Nov found no cluster under investigation for human-to-human spread, so the level stays Normal.
for_you: Avoid contact with sick or dead birds and report them to Defra. UKHSA rates the UK public risk as low.

why: H5N1 is the flu strain scientists most fear could become a pandemic; it has spread to mammals and dairy cattle.
drivers: Human cases, mammal-to-mammal spread, mutations, surveillance.
